notes: Identity verified independently from the canonical document header: title Replicating and Extending Soroka, Fournier, and Nir: Negative News Increases Arousal and Negative Affect; Roeland Dubèl, Gijs Schumacher, Maaike D. Homan, Delaney Peterson, and Bert N. Bakker; Media and Communication 2024, Volume 12, Article 7807; DOI 10.17645/mac.7807. This is the primary published research article, with methods, results, tables, discussion, and references through page 19, rather than an abstract-only parse. No PDF is supplied. Only es_value_r is assigned; all other schema fields are placeholders. The p.5 locator contains measurement/preprocessing procedures, not a unique target result. The description mentions both arousal and negative affect and does not choose an outcome, model, or test. Candidate printed results: H1 SCL negativity coefficient beta=0.019, t=0.984, p=0.325 (p.7, Table 1 p.8); H2 preregistered beta=0.038, t=1.926, p=0.054 (p.9, Table 2 p.10); exploratory H2 beta=0.060, t=13.569, p<0.001 (p.9, Table 2 p.10); H4 self-reported valence t=36.013, p<0.001 and H3 self-reported arousal t=-8.28, p<0.001 (p.10). Section 2.4 explicitly calls the coefficients z-standardised. Page 9 prose calls the 0.038 result an interaction, whereas Table 2 places it on the Negativity row; retain that discrepancy. Additional exploratory alignment correlations are rho(381)=0.03, p=0.482 and rho(357)=0.35, p<0.001 (p.11); these concern physiological/self-report alignment rather than the effect of news negativity. No candidate is promoted to the assigned effect-size value because row correspondence is unresolved. Requested r is not assumed equivalent to beta, t, or rho; no conversion or numeric matching performed. No analytic N assigned or calculated.
